pr_body:
* Shader editor is permanent (no longer transient).
* Can edit multiple files at the same time.

Likely fixes many usability issues (please lend me a hand Bugsquad team to identify them).

Obligatory gif
![shader-editor](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6265307/170669575-4773ea5e-2a74-451b-b5f8-bcbd90c7150b.gif)
pr_comments:
I'd look into adding a button to collapse the list of shaders, similar to the one we already have at the bottom of the script editor between the list and the script:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/170670673-982d53d7-469a-46b9-bf21-20743a336129.png)

This can be beneficial when editing shaders with long lines on narrow displays.

This button has a **Toggle Scripts Panel** shortcut which defaults to <kbd>Ctrl + \\</kbd>. It probably makes sense to reuse the default binding (but with a different shortcut name, I assume).

@Calinou This not easy because that section is part of the shader editor itself, and the visual shader editor does not allow placing something there. 

This is an initial implementation, other contributors can add small things to it and improve it afterwards.

> * Shader editor is permanent (no longer transient).
> * Can edit multiple files at the same time.
> 
> Likely fixes many usability issues (please lend me a hand Bugsquad team to identify them).
> 
> Obligatory gif ![shader-editor](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6265307/170669575-4773ea5e-2a74-451b-b5f8-bcbd90c7150b.gif)


Would it be possible, to add the Shader Editor's button next to the 2D/3D/Script buttons instead? And it would work like the regular script/visualscript window, except it could be split to 2 for previewing, like we can do it in 3D.

![godshad](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67164514/170675019-0b683fe9-829b-4977-bd91-c95d2ad7afa8.jpg)

@sztrovacsek92 not really, the idea of the shader editor is that you *always* edit shaders while looking at the viewport to see the changes. This is what editors on the bottom dock are for. Having it on another main tab would be very annoying, because you would need to manually split it all the time. The way it is now happens on demand.

Built-in shader names should display similar to built-in scripts, as this isn't really useful:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2223172/170699258-339aea33-553d-4687-8cba-e455c03fcfcf.png)
Also closing a scene doesn't close its built-in shaders and you can edit them on another scene, but not save.
Also also saving a built-in shader opens a save file dialog. It should save its owning scene.

@KoBeWi That makes sense and it will have to be added eventually, if you can work on improving it later on that would be great. 

I am not as familiarized to how all that logic in the editor works nowadays and it would take me longer. In general my idea is that as I have so many things pending I need to work on, I try to get something working that does what it has to do and then rely on others to bring it up to the standards they expect.

Guess I will just list some more problems that I found, but with an intention that they can be resolved later (unless it's something major):
- middle-click doesn't close shader
- File menu doesn't have any shortcut
- the option to open in the inspector is interesting, but not sure what can it be used for 🤔
- changing shader externally will force-reload it, even if you have unsaved changes. You can undo this though
- shaders have no modified state (no `(*)` appears)
- previously opened shaders aren't restored on project start
Actually it's not ok. It doesn't fix #43635, which doesn't make sense for a permanent editor.

issue_context.title: Polygon2D toolbar becomes inaccessible when a shader is attached.
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:**
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->
04103db6bd5694b81ab0a1717fc5fdde6cb5dd4f 
bfed10185a55004b258eaad7fbb3e6049448edf9 (Slightly different behavior.  Works initially.)


**OS/device including version:**
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->
Win 10 64bit

**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
When attaching a material and then a shader to a Polygon2D the toolbar to edit the points will disappear.

![godot windows tools 64_QSbit9iC8y](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13004169/99510068-4636f100-298f-11eb-828b-340b6a8556af.png)
![godot windows tools 64_CWXapGmKIV](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13004169/99510160-64045600-298f-11eb-8b23-e2c6dd8fcc23.png)



**Steps to reproduce:**
It appears to be the result of the shader text editor opening.  In 3.2 this is forced every time the Polygon2D is selected.

In the Master it seems to be fine on first selection, but after opening the shader resource and having the editor to appear, the toolbars then vanishes from then on.

1. Create a Polygon2D
2. Attach a Material and a Shader.
3. Open the Shader resource into its text editor.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
[Poly Tools Missing.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5559007/Poly.Tools.Missing.zip)
comments: I'm not sure if this should be considered a bug? After some testing it looks like it is a default Godot response after selecting an editable resource from the currently inspected object. Similar result could be observed in Polygon2D if you would try to open its texture. I even tested it with Sprite2D and, as expected, it hid its type-specific toolbar panel as well.
This will be fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/45085 once it's merged.

review_comments: I don't mind it, but I never agreed to it. I don't generally like to do this because it makes the code more difficult to read (! in one side and is_empy() on the other). Performance argument here makes little sense anyway.
If you wanted to do this properly, I would probably add also an is_not_empty() function. We have this with `RID` and `Ref<>` (`is_null()` and `is_valid()`)
I added a comment on #43181 in hopes to find a middle ground.

What's the point of this container if it has only one element?
If the button stretches without this, you can use size flags.

I find it more difficult to understand purpose using the size flags and if somebody wants to add something to where File is (like eventually a collapse button as suggested by @Calinou ) it needs to undo that code.
Doesn't LocalVector have range iterator? Also why is it LocalVector? 🤔
I generally don't use the range iterators on arrays. LocalVector is prefered if you are not passing the array around because its simpler and more efficient.

```suggestion
		shader_list->set_item_tooltip(-1, path);
```
You can use this shorthand.

Nice, did not know this was implemented here too. But, to be honest, it's not really very universal. You can see the code below: 
```
shader_tabs->set_current_tab(shader_tabs->get_tab_count() - 1);
```
Can't be written the same way, so this is quite confusing. I would ensure that this works everywhere it matters before using that syntax.

```suggestion
		file_menu->get_popup()->set_item_disabled(file_menu->get_popup()->get_item_index(i), edited_shaders.is_empty());
```
Also pretty sure the `get_item_index()` part is not necessary, as the indices should match the ids.
They do not because there are separators.
Why is this method no longer const?

It does not make sense to be const, since you are requesting internal state of the class. C++ allows this to be const because it has no idea if a pointer is internal state or not, but it does not make much sense in practice to use it for this.
